_comment: Environment adapter: the vanilla element damage keywords on every effect that deals that damage.
Rain Extinguishes Fires, Water Douses Fire, Sneak Tools, DISDD, Elementally Reactive Waters, Ice is
Slick and SIM (Simply Immersive Materials) ask whether the effect that hit carries MagicDamageFire,
MagicDamageFrost or MagicDamageShock. Modded damage spells often lack them on some effects, or on all.
vanilla.json gives the keyword to one effect of a spell that has none; these "damage" lines give it to
every effect of the spell that really deals that damage (docs/librarian/PERK_ADAPTERS.md 6-5):
the effect's own record says so: detrimental, magnitude > 0, resisted by the element's resistance
(FireResist, FrostResist, ElectricResist), a value modifier on Health or a visible Script effect.
A MagicResist or unresisted effect is not called fire, nor is Absorb, a hidden script (a perk's fear
check) or an effect with the unspecified-damage mark (keywordsNone)
the spell's catalog element rests on the record (tierMin manual: mgef or manual evidence), not on a
framework keyword alone (KIT/OCF/ADAR names: Desecration's necrotic flames are not fire)
every item using the effect is a spell this line picks (a scroll, staff, enchantment or another spell
blocks it)
In a load order with SkyPatcher Keyword Framework (MKF_DamageTypes.ini) every such value modifier has the
keyword already (TAKEALOOK 2026-10-20: nothing left to add); without it, 24 fire, 5 frost and 6 shock
effects lacked it there, 7 / 1 / 1 of them beyond what vanilla.json's one-effect lines give.
Perk mods read the same keywords: a spell that gains MagicDamageFire on another effect is boosted by the
fire perks on that effect too. That is the perk mods' intent for real fire damage, but it changes
balance for those spells (CHANGELOG).
Off with config.json "environment": { "enabled": false }.
perkMod: environment mods reading the vanilla element keywords
